alexa: Quick check — I'm adding TGW route propagation to the private route tables in us-west-2 for the new k8s worker subnets. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pull/1892. Does propagation alone add routes to the RTs or do we need explicit aws_route_table_association changes when the RTs already exist? Also thinking about NAT failover — we want per-AZ NAT preference but cross-AZ fallback. Any gotchas?

chris: Propagation only imports routes from the TGW into the TGW route table. It doesn't change VPC route tables. If your RTs already exist and are associated to subnets, no new association resource needed. If you're creating new RTs you still need aws_route_table_association.

marta: For Terraform, add aws_ec2_transit_gateway_route_table_propagation. Example snippet:```resource "aws_ec2_transit_gateway_route_table_propagation" "prop" {
  transit_gateway_route_table_id = aws_ec2_transit_gateway_route_table.main.id
  transit_gateway_attachment_id  = aws_ec2_transit_gateway_vpc_attachment.att.id
}
```If ordering is flaky, add depends_on or explicit lifecycle hooks.

sean: One thing: watch implicit route conflicts. TGW shouldn't advertise 0.0.0.0/0, but if you have a default route to a NAT gateway in the RT and some other automation adds routes, it's messy. Also test the case where AZ NAT is unhealthy — ensure connectivity still works across AZs.

alexa: We're not advertising default. TGW only shares VPC CIDRs. Main worry is per-AZ NAT swap. Ideally prefer local NAT gw, but allow fallback. What's the simplest pattern?

kim: Keep per-AZ route tables with 0.0.0.0/0 -> local NAT. For fallback, relying on AWS to route across AZs works but adds latency/cost. If you need deterministic failover, you'll need extra logic (lambda/state) to re-associate subnets or flip routes.

marta: Also in TF, to avoid noisy diffs when TGW propagates routes into the VPC route table, consider:```lifecycle {
  ignore_changes = [ routes ]
}
```That hides TGW-propagated route churn from TF plans. But be careful — it can hide real manual changes too.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: PR 1892 opened by alexa — terraform plan posted. (check: infra-staging) :white_check_mark:

sean: I'll take a look at the PR later today. Two suggestions: 1) add a small integration test that simulates AZ failover in staging, 2) tag new resources with `team:eng-infra` and `redwood:env` for cost/tracking.

alexa: Thanks — updated PR with propagation resource + lifecycle ignore for routes, and added tags. I also pasted the plan output: ```+ aws_ec2_transit_gateway_route_table_propagation.prop (new)``` @sean can you review when you have time?

chris: :eyes: will review after lunch. One nit: please include the region in resource tags (e.g., `region=us-west-2`) so billing queries are easier.

marta: Also double-check any SG references — avoid AZ-specific subnet IDs in security group rules or modules, prefer referencing by name or tags.

alexa: Closing the loop — PR merged and applied to staging. Staging smoke shows normal egress and no regressions. Will run an AZ failover canary next week and report back. Thanks everyone! :tada:
